taxonomyNote: 'Kentucky spring salamander' is a regional name; NatureServe and ADW treat the species as Spring Salamander (G. porphyriticus) and some authors lump related Gyrinophilus species into it.
fieldMarks: Large: 12-19 cm, females about 1 cm longer than males.
Salmon-orange to yellowish skin with a brownish tint and dark blotchy spots and a reddish tint.
Flat head with eyes on the sides and a broad snout.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal; swims eel-like with legs held to the body and escapes by burrowing into mud or swimming.
Uses smell to locate prey in the dark; produces toxic skin secretions as defense.
Females stay with 20-60 (up to 100+) eggs about 3 months; larvae are aquatic for 2-4 years.
habitat: Small clear upland streams, springs, caves and shaded seepages; often under rocks, logs, leaves or moss in or near water.
range: Southern Quebec and southern Maine south through the Appalachians to northern Georgia, Alabama and northeastern Mississippi.

lookalikes.name: Northern dusky salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Much smaller and browner with a keeled tail and no salmon-orange colour.
